subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should this issue stay open as the broader intermittent `workspace-sandbox` cold-start bug while the wedged-Docker timeout work is handled separately, or should maintainers fold it into the linked Docker-timeout path once that path is repaired and proven?
rationale: Current source proves an unbounded Docker wait path, but the report’s timings may also involve prune, workspace layout, Docker user resolution, or OrbStack VM cold-start behavior; only maintainers can choose the product boundary and default timeout/fail-soft behavior.

options.title: Keep Broad Issue Open
options.body: Track this issue as the broader cold-start sandbox-prep failure and use the linked timeout PR only as a partial candidate for the Docker-control-plane subpath.

options.title: Canonicalize To Docker Timeout
options.body: After the linked timeout work is repaired, proven, and merged, close this issue only if logs or proof show the observed stall was the same Docker no-timeout root cause.

options.title: Request Fresh Live Repro First
options.body: Ask for fresh redacted OrbStack logs or a live repro before choosing whether to repair this issue separately from the Docker timeout work.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Issue Open
recommendation.body: Track this issue as the broader cold-start sandbox-prep failure and use the linked timeout PR only as a partial candidate for the Docker-control-plane subpath.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to sandbox architecture, prune/runtime cleanup, and the current implicated file wrapper commit, making them the best available owner for the product/default boundary choice.
